title: Python Files, Modules and Environments: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision of reading and writing files with open(), modes, encoding and pathlib, then how Python code is organised into modules and packages and isolated with venv and pip.

chapters.title: Files and Modules at a Glance
points: open() returns a file object tied to an OS file handle; a with block closes it for you
Text mode gives str and decodes bytes; binary mode gives raw bytes
A module is one .py file; a package is a folder of modules
Imports run the module once and cache it in sys.modules
venv gives each project its own interpreter and site-packages; pip installs into the active one

chapters.title: open(), Modes and Encoding
points: Mode letters: r read (default), w truncate and write, a append, x create or fail, + read and write
Add t (text, default) or b (binary): 'rb' returns bytes, 'r' returns str
Always pass encoding='utf-8' in text mode; the default is platform dependent (often cp1252 on Windows)
w erases the file at open time, before you write anything; use a to keep existing content
Text mode translates newlines; pass newline='' for csv files

chapters.title: with Blocks and Reading Patterns
points: with open(p) as f: calls f.close() on exit, even when an exception is raised
for line in f: streams one line at a time with constant memory; f.read() loads everything
f.read(n), f.readline() and f.readlines() differ: chunk, one line, list of all lines
Lines keep their trailing \n; strip with line.rstrip('\n')
Open two files in one statement: with open(a) as src, open(b, 'w') as dst:

chapters.title: pathlib Essentials
points: Path('data') / 'in.txt' joins with / and uses the right separator on every OS
Inspect with p.exists(), p.is_file(), p.is_dir(); parts are p.name, p.stem, p.suffix, p.parent
p.read_text(encoding='utf-8') and p.write_text(s, encoding='utf-8') replace open for small files
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) creates nested folders; p.glob('*.py') and p.rglob('*.py') search
pathlib vs os.path: Path is an object with methods, os.path works on plain strings; Path.cwd() and Path(__file__).parent anchor paths

chapters.title: Imports, Packages, __main__, venv and pip
points: import m, from m import x and import m as alias; avoid from m import * because it hides where names come from
if __name__ == '__main__': runs only when the file is executed directly, not when imported; run modules with python -m pkg.mod
A folder with __init__.py is a regular package; it runs on import and can re-export names; use relative imports like from . import util
Circular imports and a local file named like a stdlib module (random.py) are the classic import errors
python -m venv .venv, then activate (.venv\Scripts\activate on Windows, source .venv/bin/activate elsewhere); never commit .venv
pip install pkg, pip install -r requirements.txt, pip freeze > requirements.txt, pip list; use python -m pip so it targets the right interpreter

chapters.title: Files, Imports and Environments Cheat Sheet
points: Modes: r w a x, + for both, b for binary; always encoding='utf-8' in text mode
Read: for line in f (stream), f.read() (all); Path.read_text() for small files
pathlib: Path(a) / b, exists, mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True), glob, rglob
Imports: guard scripts with if __name__ == '__main__'; packages need __init__.py; run with python -m pkg.mod
Env: python -m venv .venv, activate, python -m pip install -r requirements.txt, pip freeze > requirements.txt
